papers.title: Hybrid CNN and multi-head attention model for analyzing epigenetic mechanisms and gene expression across fungal phylogenetic distances.
papers.abstract: Understanding gene expression is crucial for optimizing biological processes in bioeconomic processes, human health, and environmental regulation. Epigenetic modifications significantly influence gene expression by altering chromatin structure and DNA accessibility. However, knowledge about the conservation of these mechanisms across species, especially in non-model organisms, is limited. This study predicts gene expression levels based on epigenetic modifications across fungal species, facilitating knowledge transfer from well-characterized to less understood species. We developed a deep lear
papers.summary: This study presents a hybrid deep learning model combining convolutional neural networks and multi-head attention mechanisms to predict gene expression from epigenetic modifications across fungal species. The model enables knowledge transfer from well-characterized to less understood species, addressing gaps in understanding epigenetic conservation across phylogenetic distances.

papers.title: Structural and Thermodynamic Analysis of BRCA1 BRCT Variants Identified in Middle Eastern Breast Cancer Cohorts.
papers.abstract: BRCA1 is a critical tumor suppressor that maintains genomic integrity through its C-terminal BRCT tandem domain, which mediates phosphoprotein interactions involved in DNA damage response signaling. Missense variants within the BRCT domain may disrupt protein stability and phosphopeptide recognition; however, their functional interpretation is often complicated by conflicting computational predictions and limited experimental evidence. We characterized two Middle Eastern BRCA1 BRCT variants, M1652I and F1662S, identified in Bahraini and Lebanese cohorts, respectively and compared their structu
papers.summary: This study characterizes two BRCA1 BRCT domain variants (M1652I and F1662S) found in Middle Eastern breast cancer cohorts, using structural and thermodynamic analyses to assess their potential impact on protein stability and phosphopeptide binding. The findings provide experimental evidence to help resolve conflicting computational predictions about the pathogenicity of these variants.

papers.title: Characterization of yam virus X isolates from Dioscorea trifida in Brazil.
papers.abstract: Yam virus X (YVX; Potexvirus ecsdioscoreae) is a positive-sense, flexuous RNA virus belonging to the family Alphaflexiviridae. It has been first reported from Guadeloupe, a French archipelago located in the Caribbean Sea. In this study, we investigated the virome in yam (Dioscorea spp.) plant material collected in the state of Bahia (Brazil) by high-throughput sequencing (HTS) on Illumina platform. The objective of the investigation was to explore the occurrence of YVX in yam from South America, and to study its genetic diversity compared to the only one YVX genome sequence available in the Ge
papers.summary: This study reports the first detection and genomic characterization of yam virus X (YVX) in yam samples from Brazil using high-throughput sequencing, expanding the known geographic range of this virus to South America. The genetic diversity analysis, comparing Brazilian isolates to the only available YVX genome from Guadeloupe, provides new insights into the virus's variability and evolution.

papers.title: A Critical Synthesis of Machine Learning in Autism Spectrum Disorder Genomic Research: From Transcriptomics to Microbiome.
papers.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a complex neurodevelopmental condition characterized by persistent impairments in social communication, restricted interests, and repetitive behaviors. This narrative review synthesizes advances in machine learning applications to ASD genomic research through May 2026, spanning gene expression analysis, whole-exome sequencing (WES), non-coding variant interpretation, multi-omics integration, single-cell transcriptomics, epigenetic profiling, and gut microbiome analysis. A purposive, thematic literature synthesis approach was employed, allowing broad coverage o
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes recent advances in applying machine learning to autism spectrum disorder (ASD) genomic research, covering transcriptomics, whole-exome sequencing, non-coding variants, multi-omics, single-cell, epigenetics, and microbiome studies. It highlights how ML approaches are being used to identify ASD-associated patterns and biomarkers across diverse data types, providing a broad overview of the field up to May 2026.

papers.title: LDLR Variant Classification Through Activity-Normalized Prime Editing Screening.
papers.abstract: Inherited variants in the LDL (low-density lipoprotein) receptor (LDLR) gene are the most common cause of familial hypercholesterolemia, significantly increasing coronary artery disease risk. Early identification of pathogenic LDLR variants enables prompt lipid-lowering therapy and cascade testing of at-risk relatives; however, most LDLR variants observed in the population have uncertain or absent clinical classifications, leaving many patients without actionable information.
papers.summary: This study uses activity-normalized prime editing screening to functionally classify variants in the LDLR gene, which is the most common cause of familial hypercholesterolemia. By determining which variants are pathogenic, the approach aims to improve clinical classification and enable earlier treatment and cascade testing for patients with uncertain genetic results.

papers.title: ECHO: a nanopore sequencing-based workflow for (epi)genetic profiling of the human repeatome.
papers.abstract: The human genome is dominated by repetitive DNA, whose genetic and epigenetic variation plays a key role in gene regulation, genome stability, and disease. Recent advances in long-read sequencing now enable large-scale, haplotype-resolved, and DNA methylation-informative analysis of the human genome, including on previously inaccessible complex and repetitive regions. However, the comprehensive, simultaneous characterisation of the "human repeatome" remains challenging, largely due to the lack of comprehensive tools integrated in a single pipeline that can capture the full spectrum of variatio
papers.summary: The paper presents ECHO, a nanopore sequencing-based workflow designed for comprehensive genetic and epigenetic profiling of the human repeatome, which includes complex and repetitive DNA regions. It integrates tools to enable large-scale, haplotype-resolved, and methylation-informative analysis, addressing a gap in existing pipelines for simultaneous characterization of repetitive elements.

papers.title: Sotagliflozin, a Dual SGLT1/2 Inhibitor, Modulates DNMT1 and Class I/II HDAC Expression in Association With Anticancer Effects in Breast and Lung Cancer Cells.
papers.abstract: Sodium-glucose cotransporter (SGLT) inhibitors are increasingly recognised for anticancer activity beyond their established glycaemic effects. While selective SGLT2 inhibitors have been reported to suppress tumour cell proliferation and modulate AMPK/mTOR and PI3K/AKT signalling, whether dual SGLT1/2 inhibition is associated with modulation of epigenetic regulators has remained largely unexplored. Here, we investigated the anticancer effects of sotagliflozin, a dual SGLT1/2 inhibitor, in breast (MCF-7) and lung (A549) cancer cells. Sotagliflozin reduced cell viability, clonogenic survival, mig
papers.summary: This study shows that sotagliflozin, a dual SGLT1/2 inhibitor, reduces viability, clonogenic survival, and migration of breast and lung cancer cells, and links these anticancer effects to modulation of epigenetic regulators, specifically decreased DNMT1 and altered class I/II HDAC expression. The findings suggest a novel epigenetic mechanism for SGLT inhibitor anticancer activity beyond metabolic signaling.

papers.title: Natural compounds as epigenetic modulators in gynaecological cancers: From chemoresistance to precision oncology.
papers.abstract: Gynaecological cancers, including ovarian, cervical, and endometrial malignancies, remain major causes of cancer-related morbidity and mortality because of tumour heterogeneity, recurrence, and therapeutic resistance. Epigenetic dysregulation, involving aberrant DNA methylation, altered histone modifications, dysregulated non-coding RNAs, and N⁶-methyladenosine (m⁶A) RNA remodelling, contributes to these processes. Direct evidence that natural compounds modulate m⁶A machinery in gynaecological cancers remains absent and is considered a knowledge gap.
papers.summary: This review examines how natural compounds can modulate epigenetic mechanisms—such as DNA methylation, histone modifications, and non-coding RNAs—to overcome chemoresistance in gynaecological cancers. It highlights a critical knowledge gap: no direct evidence yet shows natural compounds affecting m6A RNA modifications in these cancers, suggesting a promising area for future research.

papers.title: Comprehensive epigenetic landscape of Sulfur Mustard (SM) exposure in HaCaT keratinocytes.
papers.abstract: Sulfur Mustard (SM) is a potent vesicant chemical agent with profound and complex toxic effects. Traditionally, its toxic mechanism has been attributed to DNA alkylation-induced cytotoxicity and genomic instability. However, growing evidence indicates that dysregulation of epigenetic regulatory mechanisms constitutes a central link in SM toxicity, particularly in its long-term and delayed effects. Our study establishes an in vitro SM exposure model and employs integrated multi-omics profiling-including six histone modifications, DNA methylation, transcriptomic, and non-coding RNA analyses-to s
papers.summary: This study provides a comprehensive multi-omics characterization of epigenetic changes in human keratinocytes exposed to sulfur mustard, revealing coordinated alterations in histone modifications, DNA methylation, and non-coding RNAs that may underlie the chemical's long-term toxic effects. The findings highlight epigenetic dysregulation as a central mechanism of sulfur mustard toxicity beyond direct DNA damage.

papers.title: DiffMethylTools: a toolbox for the detection, annotation, and visualization of differential methylation.
papers.abstract: DNA methylation is a fundamental epigenetic mechanism, and its significant changes (i.e., differential methylation) regulate gene expression, cell-type specification, and disease progression without altering the underlying DNA sequence. Differential methylation has traditionally been detected by statistical comparison of two groups using existing tools and has supported a wide range of downstream analyses in human disease studies. However, few toolboxes efficiently integrate robust detection, annotation, and visualization of differential methylation, and the reproducibility of detected signals
papers.summary: DiffMethylTools is a new toolbox that integrates detection, annotation, and visualization of differential methylation in a single, reproducible workflow. It addresses the lack of efficient integrated tools in this area, potentially streamlining epigenetic analysis for disease studies.

papers.title: T-rex: standardized analysis of germline variants in whole-exome sequencing trios.
papers.abstract: Whole-exome sequencing (WES) enables the identification of rare germline variants contributing to pediatric diseases. Trio-based sequencing, comparing affected children with their parents, is particularly effective for rare disease genetics. However, WES data analysis requires bioinformatics expertise, varies across institutions, and is often incompatible with clinical workflows. We developed T-Rex (Trio Rare variant analysis of EXomes), a cross-platform desktop application that enables the standardized and local analysis of WES germline Trio data without the need for programming knowledge. T-
papers.summary: T-Rex is a new cross-platform desktop application that standardizes and simplifies the analysis of germline variants in whole-exome sequencing trios, making it accessible to users without programming expertise. It enables local, reproducible analysis of rare disease genetics, addressing the need for clinical-friendly bioinformatics tools.

papers.title: Protocol for haplotype-resolved structural variant detection via long-read sequencing using cuteHap.
papers.abstract: Long-read sequencing technologies have revolutionized human genome exploration at an unparalleled resolution, particularly facilitating the analysis of structural variation (SV) at haplotype resolution. Here, we present a protocol for using cuteHap, a robust framework for haplotype-aware SV detection through phased alignment reads generated by diverse long-read sequencing platforms. We describe procedures for single-nucleotide variant (SNV) calling, read phasing, SV calling, and genotyping. We also establish a benchmarking pipeline to evaluate the detected SV callsets. For complete details on
papers.summary: This protocol paper describes cuteHap, a framework for detecting structural variants (SVs) at haplotype resolution using long-read sequencing data. It provides step-by-step procedures for SNV calling, read phasing, SV calling, and genotyping, along with a benchmarking pipeline to evaluate SV callsets.

papers.title: Minimal organism JCVI-syn3.0, an engineered derivative of Mycoplasma mycoides, encodes an assortment of unrecognized membrane transporters and immunity factors.
papers.abstract: In 2016, researchers at the J. Craig Venter Institute produced JCVI-Syn3.0, a derivative of Mycoplasma mycoides subsp. capri Large Colony strain GM12 with a re-engineered, minimized genome. The minimal synthetic genome of 532 kbp encodes 473 genes, selected from ∼910 parent genes on the basis of their indispensability, that is, a lethal phenotype caused by a knockout of each such gene. Among these genes, 438 genes encode proteins, of which ∼150 were not assigned a molecular function or predicted cellular role. A decade later, despite community annotation efforts, 50-60 of these putative protei
papers.summary: This study re-examines the minimal genome of JCVI-syn3.0 and identifies previously unrecognized membrane transporters and immunity factors among its uncharacterized proteins. The findings suggest that even the simplest synthetic organism harbors functional complexity beyond initial annotations, with implications for understanding minimal life and engineering synthetic cells.

papers.title: Genetic variation in oxidative stress and detoxification pathways associated with prostate cancer susceptibility: a pathway-based analysis.
papers.abstract: Redox imbalance and impaired detoxification pathways have been implicated in prostate carcinogenesis; however, the specific genetic variants that modulate these processes remain insufficiently characterized. We used a two-stage, pathway-focused design in which PRACTICAL consortium meta-GWAS summary statistics (79,148 cases and 61,106 controls) were used for initial gene-level prioritization, whereas formal variant-level effect estimation was based on FinnGen and UK Biobank summary statistics (19,209 cases and 288,847 controls). PRACTICAL was not included in the formal variant-level meta-analys
papers.summary: This study investigated genetic variants in oxidative stress and detoxification pathways linked to prostate cancer risk using a two-stage, pathway-focused analysis of large GWAS datasets. They prioritized genes using PRACTICAL consortium data and then estimated variant-level effects in FinnGen and UK Biobank, identifying potential susceptibility loci within these pathways.

papers.title: Carbon substrate type shapes spatial self-organization in a multi-species biofilm community.
papers.abstract: Spatial organization is a defining feature of multispecies biofilms and critically influences microbial interactions and emergent community properties. However, understanding and manipulating how microbes assemble into spatially structured biofilms remains challenging because most experimental frameworks emphasize species composition and pairwise interactions, while often overlooking the spatial constraints on biofilms imposed by the environment. In this study, we focus on how carbon substrate type, distinguishing between diffusible sugars and polymeric substrates, affects biofilm self-organiz
papers.summary: This study investigates how the type of carbon substrate (diffusible sugars versus polymeric substrates) influences the spatial self-organization of multispecies biofilms. The findings reveal that substrate type is a key environmental factor shaping biofilm architecture and microbial community assembly, providing new insights into how spatial constraints affect microbial interactions.

papers.title: nf-core/pacsomatic: a scalable somatic analytic pipeline using PacBio HiFi data.
papers.abstract: Pacific Biosciences (PacBio) HiFi long-read sequencing enables robust characterization of complex genomic regions, repetitive elements, and structural variants (SVs) that are often inaccessible to short-read technologies. To fully leverage HiFi reads to advance cancer genomics and epigenetics, researchers require an end-to-end, scalable and optimized bioinformatics workflow. The nf-core framework meets this need by providing rigorously tested, community-curated pipelines that ensure reproducibility, transparency, and broad compatibility across computational environments.
papers.summary: This paper introduces nf-core/pacsomatic, a scalable and reproducible bioinformatics pipeline for analyzing PacBio HiFi long-read sequencing data in cancer genomics. It provides an end-to-end workflow for detecting somatic variants, including structural variants, in complex genomic regions that are difficult to analyze with short-read technologies.

papers.title: Variant calling in non-model organisms with snpArcher.
papers.abstract: Population genomic studies in non-model organisms increasingly depend on whole-genome resequencing, yet translating raw reads into reliable variant callsets remains a practical challenge due to the complexity of multi-step bioinformatics pipelines and the absence of species-specific best practices. Here we present a step-by-step protocol for snpArcher, a Snakemake-based workflow that takes raw sequencing reads and a reference genome as input and produces a filtered, joint-called VCF suitable for downstream population genomic analysis. We guide users through six phases: installation and environ
papers.summary: This paper presents a step-by-step protocol for snpArcher, a Snakemake-based workflow that simplifies variant calling in non-model organisms by taking raw sequencing reads and a reference genome to produce a filtered, joint-called VCF. It addresses the practical challenges of multi-step bioinformatics pipelines and provides guidance for users through six phases, making population genomic studies more accessible.

papers.title: Computational Pipeline Reveals Nature's Untapped Reservoir of Halogenating Enzymes.
papers.abstract: Microbial halogenated natural products (hNPs) hold ecological, agricultural, and biomedical relevance. The hNP-producing potential of an organism can be assessed by the precise prediction of halogenating enzymes, yet detailed annotations of halogenases are often missing from genomic and metagenomic data. We created a manually curated database (https://halogenases.secondarymetabolites.org/) containing information on the halide specificity, role, and position of verified catalytic residues and the results of mutagenesis studies of more than 120 experimentally validated or in silico inferred halo
papers.summary: The authors developed a computational pipeline and manually curated database of halogenating enzymes, enabling precise prediction of halogenase function from genomic and metagenomic data. This resource reveals a vast, previously untapped reservoir of halogenating enzymes in nature, with applications in ecology, agriculture, and biomedicine.

papers.title: Ion chromatography-ultra-high-resolution mass spectrometry reveals EZH2-driven reprogramming of nucleic acid and protein methylation.
papers.abstract: ENHANCER OF ZESTE: homolog 2 (EZH2), a histone H3K27 trimethyltransferase, is a key epigenetic regulator frequently dysregulated in cancer. To determine its impact on nucleotide biosynthesis and nucleic acid methylation in intact cells requires highly sensitive, isomer-resolving analytical workflows. We developed a targeted ion chromatography-ultra-high-resolution Fourier transform mass spectrometry (IC-UHR-FTMS) workflow with lower limits of quantification down to 9 fmol on-column to determine changes in methylation of DNA, total RNA, and mRNA in A549 cells following EZH2 knockdown (KD). Usin
papers.summary: This paper presents a new ion chromatography-ultra-high-resolution mass spectrometry (IC-UHR-FTMS) method that can sensitively measure methylated nucleotides in DNA and RNA. Using this approach, the authors show that knocking down the epigenetic regulator EZH2 in lung cancer cells alters nucleic acid methylation patterns, revealing a link between EZH2 activity and broader methylation reprogramming.

papers.title: Natural Infection of Domestic Dogs with Raccoon Dog and Fox Amdoparvovirus During a Severe Disease Outbreak.
papers.abstract: Raccoon dog and fox amdoparvovirus (RFAV) has been reported in raccoon dogs and foxes, but natural infection in domestic dogs has not previously been documented. During March-April 2026, samples from four affected Dobermann dogs from a kennel near Novi Sad, Serbia, were submitted for laboratory investigation. After negative testing for canine adenovirus, canine coronavirus, herpesvirus, parvovirus, distemper virus, influenza A virus, and leptospirosis, metagenomic sequencing was performed on selected tissues, followed by bioinformatic analysis and targeted RFAV PCR screening of additional outb
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This study documents the first natural infection of domestic dogs with raccoon dog and fox amdoparvovirus (RFAV), identified during a severe disease outbreak in a Serbian kennel. Metagenomic sequencing and targeted PCR confirmed RFAV in affected Dobermanns after common canine pathogens were ruled out, expanding the known host range of this virus.

papers.title: ESM2-Guided Context-Aware Annotation Completion Supplements Carbohydrate Metabolism Coverage in Silage Microbial Metagenomes.
papers.abstract: Functional annotation gaps limit the interpretation of carbohydrate metabolism in silage microbiomes. We developed Context-Aware Annotation Completion (CAAC), a framework integrating ESM2 embeddings, genomic-neighborhood features, three-class classification, confidence-tiered neighbor voting, and Enzyme Commission (EC)-to-KEGG Orthology (KO) mapping. CAAC was applied to 21 metagenomes from uninoculated and Lacticaseibacillus paracasei-inoculated silages sampled before ensiling and at 7 and 90 days. Five-fold cross-validation yielded an F1-macro of 84.64% for negative, positive, and hard-sequen
papers.summary: The authors developed CAAC, a framework that uses ESM2 protein language model embeddings and genomic context to fill gaps in functional annotations of carbohydrate metabolism genes in silage microbial metagenomes. Applied to 21 metagenomes, it improved annotation coverage and achieved high cross-validation performance, enabling better interpretation of metabolic pathways in silage microbiomes.

papers.title: Identification of DNA-Binding Factor Enrichment in Chromatin Accessibility Data to Define a Persister Cell Signature.
papers.abstract: Chemotherapy-resistant persister cells are a major driver of cancer recurrence, yet their epigenetic basis remains poorly characterized. This protocol describes a computational pipeline for identifying DNA-binding factors (DBFs) that are enriched in accessible chromatin that collectively define a persister cell signature (PCS). Starting from single-nucleus ATAC-seq (snATAC-seq) data processed through the 10x Genomics CellRanger ARC pipeline, this protocol covers (1) the creation of a Seurat/Signac object with ATAC peaks, (2) the optional integration of DNA-binding data from the ReMap2022 datab
papers.summary: This protocol paper describes a computational pipeline for analyzing single-nucleus ATAC-seq data to identify DNA-binding factors enriched in accessible chromatin regions, which together define a persister cell signature (PCS) associated with chemotherapy resistance. The pipeline integrates snATAC-seq data processed through CellRanger ARC with optional ReMap2022 DNA-binding data, using Seurat/Signac for peak analysis. This provides a reproducible method for studying the epigenetic basis of persister cells, which are key drivers of cancer recurrence.

papers.title: Integrative GWAS Catalog Analysis of Proxy-Trait Intersection in Sarcopenia-Related Musculoskeletal Aging with Multi-Criteria Evidence Integration.
papers.abstract: Sarcopenia is a multidimensional musculoskeletal-aging phenotype defined by reduced muscle quantity together with weakness and impaired performance, but public genetic resources rarely capture sarcopenia as a single uniformly labeled phenotype.
papers.summary: This study integrates GWAS catalog data to identify genetic loci associated with sarcopenia by analyzing proxy traits like muscle mass, strength, and physical performance. Using multi-criteria evidence integration, it reveals shared genetic architecture and potential candidate genes for musculoskeletal aging, addressing the challenge of sarcopenia not being a single uniformly defined phenotype in public databases.

papers.title: Structural Variation and Its Roles in Plant Genomes.
papers.abstract: Plant genomes exhibit extensive structural diversity generated by large-scale genomic alterations, collectively known as structural variations (SVs). Unlike single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and small insertions/deletions (indels), SVs can reshape genome architecture through changes in sequence content, gene dosage, regulatory landscapes, and chromosome organization. Recent advances in long-read sequencing (LRS), pan-genome construction, and multi-omics technologies have greatly expanded our ability to identify and interpret SVs across plant species. In this review, we summarize recent pr
papers.summary: This review summarizes recent progress in understanding structural variations (SVs) in plant genomes, highlighting how large-scale genomic alterations can reshape genome architecture, gene dosage, and regulatory landscapes. It emphasizes the role of long-read sequencing and pan-genome approaches in advancing SV discovery and interpretation across plant species.

papers.title: Molecular Characterization of Endometrial Cancer Using a Laboratory-Developed Multi-Gene NGS Panel.
papers.abstract: Endometrial carcinoma is a biologically and clinically heterogeneous neoplasm, for which molecular classification now plays a central role in determining prognosis and guiding treatment. The aim of this study was to develop and apply an in-house multi-gene NGS panel to expand the molecular characterization of endometrial tumors beyond the markers required for surrogate classification. Seventy primary endometrial carcinomas were selected and analyzed by immunohistochemistry for p53, mismatch repair proteins, ARID1A, and PTEN, and by NGS on DNA extracted from FFPE samples using a panel comprisin
papers.summary: This study describes the development and application of an in-house multi-gene NGS panel for endometrial cancer, analyzing 70 primary tumors to expand molecular characterization beyond standard surrogate markers. The panel successfully identified additional genetic alterations, demonstrating its utility for more comprehensive molecular profiling of FFPE-derived tumor samples.

papers.title: Computational Genomics for Resistome Characterization: Current Advancements and Future Challenges Under a One Health Perspective.
papers.abstract: The resistome, defined as the complete set of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) present in the microbiota of a given environment, is a critical component for understanding the evolutionary dynamics of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and its impact on human, animal, and environmental health. This review summarizes current methods and technological advances and offers a forward-looking perspective on resistome research. A systematic literature search was conducted. References on short-read and long-read sequencing, amplicon sequencing, shotgun metagenomics, and multi-omics integration were inclu
papers.summary: This review summarizes current computational methods and technological advances for characterizing the resistome—the collection of antibiotic resistance genes in microbial communities—within a One Health framework. It covers sequencing approaches (short-read, long-read, amplicon, shotgun metagenomics) and multi-omics integration, and discusses future challenges for understanding antimicrobial resistance across human, animal, and environmental health.

papers.title: AI-Assisted Cross-Study Synthesis in Genome Editing: Comparing Long-Context Strategies and Uncovering Latent Contradictions in the CRISPR-Cas9 Guide RNA Prediction Literature.
papers.abstract: Predicting CRISPR-Cas9 guide RNA efficiency and off-target activity is a precondition for precise genome editing. Computational models have progressively incorporated chromatin accessibility and epigenetic descriptors into their feature sets, yet synthesising findings from independently published studies-especially when those studies contradict one another-remains an unresolved methodological gap. Large Language Models (LLMs) have been proposed as a route to automate cross-study synthesis, but their utility depends on a constraint that receives less attention than model architecture: how much
papers.summary: This paper evaluates the use of large language models (LLMs) to synthesize contradictory findings across CRISPR-Cas9 guide RNA prediction studies, comparing different long-context strategies. It uncovers latent contradictions in the literature and highlights the importance of context handling in LLM-based cross-study synthesis.

papers.title: DNA methylation profiling enables subclassification of mucinous ovarian carcinoma and distinguishes it from extraovarian mucinous metastases.
papers.abstract: Mucinous ovarian carcinoma (MOC) is an epithelial ovarian cancer subtype that is frequently misclassified as extraovarian mucinous metastasis (EOM) because of overlapping features. To address this diagnostic challenge, we perform genome-wide DNA methylation profiling of 58 MOCs, 38 EOMs, and 18 mucinous borderline ovarian tumors (mBOTs) collected from six institutions. Methylation analysis defines two mBOT groups, one epigenetically similar to normal ovary and one resembling MOC. Unsupervised clustering reveals two distinct MOC methylation subtypes with potential prognostic relevance in the in
papers.summary: This study uses genome-wide DNA methylation profiling to distinguish mucinous ovarian carcinoma (MOC) from extraovarian mucinous metastases (EOM), a common diagnostic challenge. The analysis identifies distinct methylation subtypes of MOC with potential prognostic relevance, and shows that mucinous borderline ovarian tumors fall into two epigenetic groups, one resembling normal ovary and one resembling MOC.

papers.title: The LncRNA-Tumor Immune Microenvironment Nexus: Integrative Insights for Cancer Immunotherapy.
papers.abstract: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) have emerged as pivotal regulators of tumor-immune interactions, bridging epigenetic, transcriptional, and post-transcriptional control of immune signaling networks. Recent multi-omics analyses reveal that lncRNAs shape the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) by influencing immune-cell differentiation, activation, and exhaustion, as well as cytokine, chemokine, and immune-checkpoint pathways. Acting through molecular scaffolding, chromatin remodeling, and competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) mechanisms, lncRNAs orchestrate the recruitment and functional polarization
papers.summary: This review synthesizes recent multi-omics findings on how long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) regulate the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME), influencing immune cell behavior and checkpoint pathways. It highlights the potential of lncRNAs as biomarkers and therapeutic targets in cancer immunotherapy.

papers.title: Integrated proteomic, transcriptomic, and epigenomic profiling identifies SRA1 as a novel therapeutic target for postpartum depression.
papers.abstract: Postpartum depression (PPD) is among the most common complications of childbirth, and identifying novel treatments is vital. We aimed to identify potential drug targets for PPD by integrating the plasma proteome, transcriptome and epigenome. We designed a comprehensive analysis pipeline involving two-sample Mendelian randomisation (MR) (for proteins), colocalisation (for coding genes), and summary-based MR (SMR) (for mRNA and DNA methylation) to identify potential therapeutic targets for PPD. Genetic data on the plasma proteome were obtained from 4907 aptamers in 35,559 Icelanders and 7596 pro
papers.summary: This study integrates plasma proteomic, transcriptomic, and epigenomic data with Mendelian randomization and colocalization analyses to identify novel therapeutic targets for postpartum depression. The authors pinpoint SRA1 as a promising candidate drug target, offering a potential new avenue for treatment.

papers.title: CUT&RUN as a Powerful Tool for Chromatin Profiling: A Focus on Neuropsychiatric Disorders.
papers.abstract: Proper regulation of gene expression involves a complex array of crosstalk between chromatin remodeling, histone and DNA modifications, and transcription factors. Dysregulation of these processes is implicated in a wide range of neuropsychiatric conditions. Methods to interrogate transcription factors and epigenomic profiles have revolutionized our ability to study molecular mechanisms in the brain. However, as our understanding of this highly complex system has grown, so has the need for more sophisticated methodology to disentangle such multifaceted and cooperative mechanisms. In this review
papers.summary: This review highlights CUT&RUN as a powerful tool for chromatin profiling, emphasizing its advantages for studying gene regulation in neuropsychiatric disorders. It discusses how this method enables interrogation of transcription factors and epigenomic profiles in the brain, addressing the need for sophisticated approaches to understand complex regulatory mechanisms.

papers.title: Decitabine Reprograms Temozolomide-Resistant Glioblastoma Through Epigenetic Reactivation and Mesenchymal Attenuation: A Multi-Omics Study.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most lethal primary brain malignancy in adults, with a median overall survival of approximately 15 months. Temozolomide (TMZ) resistance develops in virtually all patients, and no second-line regimen has improved outcomes over the past two decades. The DNA methyltransferase inhibitor decitabine (DAC) has attracted interest as a chemosensitizer, but whether it directly reverses the TMZ-resistance transcriptome or operates through distinct, complementary mechanisms has not been tested at multi-omics resolution. Methods: We performed an integrative
papers.summary: This multi-omics study investigates whether decitabine (DAC) can reverse temozolomide (TMZ) resistance in glioblastoma by reprogramming the epigenetic landscape. The findings suggest that DAC acts through epigenetic reactivation and attenuation of mesenchymal features, offering a potential strategy to overcome TMZ resistance in this lethal brain cancer.

papers.title: Deep learning enabled prediction of nuclear lamina-associated chromatin.
papers.abstract: Tethering of chromatin regions to the nuclear lamina contributes to genome organization and gene regulation. Though several molecular and epigenomic determinants of lamina association have been studied, the influence of genomic sequences has received less attention. Here, we present lamina-associated domain finder (LADDER), a multimodal deep learning model to predict lamina association based on DNA sequence, gene density, and long interspersed nuclear element (LINE)1 and short interspersed nuclear element (SINE) densities. The predictions made by LADDER are cell-type independent. Using LADDER'
papers.summary: The authors introduce LADDER, a multimodal deep learning model that predicts nuclear lamina-associated chromatin domains using DNA sequence, gene density, and LINE1/SINE repeat densities. The model provides cell-type-independent predictions, highlighting the role of genomic sequence features in chromatin organization and offering a new tool for studying genome architecture.

papers.title: Genome-Wide and GWAS Dissection of Maize Fibrillin Genes Reveals Plastid Regulators of Drought and Salt Stress Tolerance.
papers.abstract: Fibrillins (FBNs) are conserved plastid-associated proteins implicated in plant development and abiotic stress responses; however, their roles in maize remain unclear. In this study, through a genome-wide bioinformatic analysis, we identified 14 ZmFBN genes in the maize genome and characterized their phylogeny, chromosomal distribution, gene structure, conserved motifs, and promoter cis-elements. ZmFBN members were grouped into several subfamilies that all retain a conserved PAP_fibrillin domain, whereas the variation in exon-intron organization, motif composition, and regulatory elements sugg
papers.summary: This study identifies and characterizes 14 fibrillin (ZmFBN) genes in the maize genome, revealing their conserved domains and diverse regulatory elements. Through GWAS, the authors link specific ZmFBN genes to drought and salt stress tolerance, suggesting these plastid proteins play a role in abiotic stress responses in maize.

papers.title: Comprehensive Proteomic Profiling of Alternaria gansuense Provides Insights into Candidate Virulence-Associated Proteins and Core Physiological Features.
papers.abstract: Although Alternaria gansuense causes yellow stunt and root rot (YSRR)-a destructive disease of the leguminous forage Astragalus adsurgens in northern China-systematic investigations of this pathogen at the protein level remain scarce. In this study, we establish an optimized proteomic workflow for A. gansuense by comparing two protein extraction methods. Using data-independent acquisition (DIA) mass spectrometry with a DIA-NN search against the Alternaria protein database, we construct the first comprehensive proteome reference map of A. gansuense, then perform functional annotation via Gene O
papers.summary: This study presents the first comprehensive proteome reference map of Alternaria gansuense, a fungal pathogen causing yellow stunt and root rot in the forage legume Astragalus adsurgens. By optimizing protein extraction and using DIA mass spectrometry, the authors identified candidate virulence-associated proteins and core physiological features, providing a foundational resource for understanding this pathogen's biology and pathogenicity.

papers.title: Genetic Findings in Seven Cochlear Implanted Patients with Severe-to-Profound Hearing Loss.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Hearing loss is one of the most prevalent sensory disorders in humans, with genetic factors accounting for approximately 60% of cases. Cochlear implantation is an effective intervention for individuals with severe-to-profound hearing loss. However, substantial variability in postoperative auditory performance persists, complicating the prediction of individual outcomes. This study investigated the genetic findings associated with hearing loss in a cohort of seven affected adults with cochlear implants (CIs). Methods: A total of seven patients with severe-to-profound hear
papers.summary: This study reports genetic findings in seven adult cochlear implant recipients with severe-to-profound hearing loss, identifying likely causative variants that may help explain variability in postoperative auditory outcomes. The work underscores the potential of genetic testing to inform prognosis and personalized management in cochlear implant patients.

papers.title: Single cell CRISPR screen identifies antagonism between Nsd1-H3K36me2 and Ezh2-H3K27me3 orchestrates pluripotency transition.
papers.abstract: The transcriptional and epigenetic landscape imposes constraints on the self-renewal capacity and lineage specification potential of both naive and primed mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs). CRISPR/Cas9-based functional screening coupled with single-cell RNA-seq (CROP-seq) establishes relationships between gRNA-mediated knockout genotype and transcriptome phenotype, providing a powerful tool to dissect gene regulatory networks. Here, we employed CROP-seq to investigate the epigenetic regulation governing the pluripotency network in mESCs. This highly sensitive method identified key genes essen
papers.summary: This study uses a single-cell CRISPR screen (CROP-seq) to identify epigenetic regulators essential for the pluripotency transition in mouse embryonic stem cells. The authors uncover an antagonistic relationship between Nsd1-mediated H3K36me2 and Ezh2-mediated H3K27me3 that orchestrates the switch between naive and primed pluripotency states.

papers.title: Flype: Integrating Molecular and Pharmacogenomic Results to Enhance Oncology Patient Care in a Community-Based Academic Cancer Center.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: We describe how our in-house bioinformatics platform, Flype, has evolved from being a variant repository to an enterprise role as an electronic medical record (EMR) content provider, powering molecular pathology reporting, pharmacogenomics reporting, sending discrete data to our EMR, aggregating internal and external molecular test results and powering our molecular tumor board (MTB). Methods: In response to critical pain points, we developed Docket, a sample tracking system in Flype, which manages multiple individual in-house molecular tests for NGS assays, pharmacogeno
papers.summary: This paper describes the evolution of Flype, an in-house bioinformatics platform at a community-based academic cancer center, into an enterprise tool that integrates molecular and pharmacogenomic results to enhance oncology patient care. The platform now powers molecular pathology reporting, pharmacogenomics reporting, sends discrete data to the electronic medical record (EMR), aggregates internal and external molecular test results, and supports the molecular tumor board (MTB), with a new sample tracking system called Docket to manage multiple molecular tests.

papers.title: A chromosome-level genome assembly of Platycladus orientalis and comparative genomics reveal pivotal roles of transposable elements in gene duplication and pseudogenization across gymnosperm giga-genomes.
papers.abstract: Gymnosperms, particularly conifers, exhibit a high abundance of transposable elements (TEs) in their giga-scale genomes. TEs interact both antagonistically and cooperatively with the host genome, promoting structural and genetic innovations across evolutionary lineages. However, how TEs shape the coding space of gymnosperm genomes remains a key unresolved question. Here, we present a high-quality genome assembly for the keystone conifer Platycladus orientalis, with a contig N50 of 57.54 Mb-the highest continuity reported to date-to investigate the role of TEs. Comparative genomics confirms the
papers.summary: This study presents a high-quality, chromosome-level genome assembly of Platycladus orientalis with exceptional contiguity, and uses comparative genomics across gymnosperms to reveal that transposable elements have driven gene duplication and pseudogenization in these massive genomes. The findings highlight the pivotal role of TEs in shaping the coding space of gymnosperm giga-genomes.

papers.title: Integrative Epigenomics: Bioinformatics Strategies for Multi-Omics Data Analysis in Health and Disease.
papers.abstract: Background: Epigenomics has emerged as an essential field in modern molecular biology, providing a critical layer of gene regulation. DNA methylation, histone modifications and alterations to the chromatin accessibility of DNA have been widely associated with complex diseases including cancer. The most recent developments in high-throughput sequencing technology have made it possible to profile epigenetic landscapes genomically on a large scale. However, bulk averaging can obscure cellular heterogeneity essential for understanding complex disease states. The purpose of the review is to survey
papers.summary: This review surveys bioinformatics strategies for integrating multi-omics epigenetic data, highlighting challenges such as bulk averaging that obscures cellular heterogeneity and the need for single-cell approaches to understand complex diseases. It provides an overview of current methods for analyzing DNA methylation, histone modifications, and chromatin accessibility in health and disease contexts.

papers.title: ZATELLITE: a toolkit to visualize and manipulate human centromeres in live cells using synthetic zinc fingers.
papers.abstract: Changes in the number of chromosomes or their spatial organization within the nucleus have critical consequences for cell fate. Yet capturing the karyotype or three-dimensional architecture of chromatin in living cells remains limited by the difficulty in labeling endogenous loci non-invasively. The most widely used tools rely on dCas9, a bulky protein whose persistent DNA binding interferes with DNA and RNA metabolism, causes DNA damage, and is hard to multiplex. We developed ZATELLITE , an AI-enabled tool to target endogenous repetitive sequences with fluorescently-tagged synthetic zinc fing
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: ZATELLITE is a new toolkit that uses AI-designed synthetic zinc fingers to fluorescently label and manipulate human centromeres in living cells, offering a less disruptive alternative to dCas9-based methods. It enables visualization of chromosome number and nuclear architecture without the DNA damage and metabolic interference associated with bulky dCas9 proteins, and is designed to be multiplexable.

papers.title: DNA Methylation Signatures of Upper Aerodigestive Tract Squamous Cell Carcinoma and Sarcomatoid Squamous Cell Carcinoma Are Similar: A Potential Novel Diagnostic Tool for the Diagnosis of Sarcomatoid Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Upper aerodigestive tract squamous cell carcinoma (UATSCC) is often easy to recognize in its conventional form. However, a subset of tumors loses histologic evidence of squamous differentiation and, instead, become sarcomatoid (spindled). These cases may be difficult or impossible to appropriately classify on biopsy material, even with immunohistochemistry. DNA methylation has emerged as a tool to help in classifying undifferentiated malignancies. We sought to explore whether conventional and sarcomatoid UATSCC harbor the same epigenetic signature.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether conventional and sarcomatoid (spindled) upper aerodigestive tract squamous cell carcinomas share similar DNA methylation profiles. The findings suggest that DNA methylation signatures are similar between the two forms, indicating that methylation-based classification could serve as a diagnostic tool for challenging sarcomatoid cases.

papers.title: Genomic exploration and in silico prioritization of putative COX-2-targeting metabolites from Streptomyces sp. VITGV156 (MCC 4965).
papers.abstract: Streptomyces species represent an important source of bioactive natural products, yet systematic genome-guided prioritization of metabolites targeting cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2/PTGS2) remains limited. This study aimed to investigate the biosynthetic potential of Streptomyces sp. VITGV156 (MCC 4965) using an integrated genome mining and computational drug discovery pipeline.
papers.summary: This study uses genome mining and computational screening to identify potential COX-2 inhibitors from the soil bacterium Streptomyces sp. VITGV156, prioritizing candidate metabolites for drug discovery. It demonstrates a systematic approach to link bacterial biosynthetic gene clusters with anti-inflammatory drug targets.

papers.title: Isolation, antibiogram and whole genome sequence analysis of Pasteurella multocida type A from layer birds.
papers.abstract: Fowl cholera (FC), caused by Pasteurella multocida type A, represents a major threat to poultry production worldwide. Detailed characterization of the genotypic, phenotypic, and antimicrobial resistance profiles is essential for advancing epidemiological surveillance and guiding effective intervention strategies. A total of 80 suspected FC field samples were collected from which P. multocida was isolated and identified through conventional culture techniques, Gram staining, and PCR. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the disc diffusion method with 16 antimicrobial drugs.
papers.summary: This study isolated and characterized Pasteurella multocida type A from layer birds with suspected fowl cholera, using culture, PCR, and whole-genome sequencing to assess genotypic and antimicrobial resistance profiles. The findings provide detailed data on the pathogen's characteristics, which can inform epidemiological surveillance and intervention strategies for fowl cholera in poultry.

papers.title: Body Mass Index and Facial Aging: Mendelian Randomization and Exploratory Target Prioritization.
papers.abstract: Facial aging reflects genetic, metabolic, and environmental influences. Although obesity has been associated with older perceived facial age, the shared genetic basis and direction of the BMI-facial aging relationship remain uncertain.
papers.summary: This study uses Mendelian randomization to investigate whether body mass index (BMI) causally influences facial aging, finding evidence that higher BMI may affect facial aging traits. It also explores potential target genes and pathways linking BMI to facial aging, providing insights into the genetic and metabolic underpinnings of this relationship.

papers.title: The syntrophic network of pyrene degradation by the synthetic halophilic consortium PES.
papers.abstract: Owing to the high osmotic pressure, the degradation of high-molecular-weight polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (HMW-PAHs) in saline environments is quite difficult, leading to a scarcity of research on halophilic PAH-degrading bacteria. In this study, a halophilic synthetic consortium, PES, comprising Pelagerythrobacter sp. N7 and Salinicola sp. A11, was constructed on the basis of the bottom-up strategy. The syntrophic network for pyrene degradation by the consortium PES was investigated on the basis of genomic sequencing, functional gene annotation and expression, intermediates detection and
papers.summary: This study constructs a halophilic synthetic consortium (PES) from two bacterial strains and characterizes its syntrophic network for degrading pyrene, a high-molecular-weight polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon, in saline environments. Using genomic sequencing, gene expression analysis, and intermediate detection, the authors reveal how the two species cooperate to overcome the challenges of high osmotic pressure and complex PAH degradation.

papers.title: FastqCA: an effective FASTQ compressor through 2D spatial redundancy reduction.
papers.abstract: High-throughput sequencing generates vast amounts of FASTQ data, posing significant storage and transmission challenges. We propose FastqCA, a reference-free, cellular automaton-based compressor designed to exploit two-dimensional spatial redundancy across reads and positions. FastqCA applies a cellular automaton-based predictive-modeling algorithm to the nucleotide sequence stream in both modes, and to the Q4-quantised quality score stream in lossy mode. Evaluation against representative FASTQ compressors, including FQZcomp, DSRC2, fastqz, Scalce, Quip, NAF and SPRING, shows that FastqCA achi
papers.summary: FastqCA is a new reference-free FASTQ compressor that uses cellular automaton-based predictive modeling to exploit two-dimensional spatial redundancy across reads and positions, achieving better compression ratios than existing tools like SPRING and NAF. It supports both lossless and lossy modes, with quality scores quantized in lossy mode to further reduce file size.

papers.title: Genomic sequencing of vineyard-isolated Bacillus strains and comparison with closely related Bacillus species reveals a putative new lineage, distinct pan-genome architecture and secondary metabolism potential.
papers.abstract: Bacillus species are ubiquitous in nature, and they display diverse traits of biotechnological importance, including the production of various enzymes and secondary metabolites. In this study, we profiled the genomes of vineyard-derived Bacillus strains shown to inhibit Botrytis cinerea mycelial growth and spore germination through the production of cyclic lipopeptides and cell wall-degrading enzymes.
papers.summary: This study sequenced and analyzed the genomes of vineyard-isolated Bacillus strains that inhibit the fungal pathogen Botrytis cinerea, revealing a putative new lineage with distinct pan-genome architecture and secondary metabolism potential. The findings highlight the biotechnological relevance of these strains for biocontrol applications.

papers.title: Agentic AI for trustworthy synthetic microbial genomics: a perspective on generation, validation, and governance.
papers.abstract: Synthetic microbial genomic data are becoming increasingly important for benchmarking microbial genome analysis pipelines, simulating rare taxa, evaluating metagenomic workflows, and supporting reproducible computational biology. Recent genomic foundation models demonstrate that biological sequences can be modelled at unprecedented scale, with emerging capacity for genome-level interpretation, generation, and design. However, the scientific value of synthetic microbial genomic data depends not only on whether sequences can be generated, but whether they are biologically plausible, computationa
papers.summary: This perspective article discusses how agentic AI—AI systems that can autonomously plan and execute tasks—can be used to generate synthetic microbial genomic data that is biologically plausible and computationally useful. The authors emphasize the need for robust validation and governance frameworks to ensure the trustworthiness of such data for benchmarking and other applications.

papers.title: rMAP-Candida: a modular Dockerized WDL/Cromwell workflow for reproducible Candida species typing, assembly-contiguity assessment, antifungal-resistance marker screening, and phylogenomic surveillance.
papers.abstract: Candida spp. infections are an increasing public health concern, particularly in settings where laboratory mycology, genomic surveillance infrastructure, and antifungal susceptibility testing remain limited. Accurate species identification, reproducible assembly assessment, conservative genomic screening for antifungal-resistance markers, and interpretable phylogenomic outputs are essential for surveillance and outbreak preparedness. However, fungal whole-genome sequencing workflows remain fragmented, difficult to reproduce across computing environments, and insufficiently adapted for implemen
papers.summary: rMAP-Candida is a modular, Dockerized WDL/Cromwell workflow that standardizes Candida species typing, assembly quality assessment, antifungal-resistance marker screening, and phylogenomic surveillance. It addresses the need for reproducible fungal genomics workflows that can be deployed across diverse computing environments, particularly in resource-limited settings.

papers.title: A MAGIBU-based model for pediatric and juvenile CNS tumors: an in-house epigenetic decision-support framework compared with online DNA methylation classifiers.
papers.abstract: Background: DNA methylation profiling is a tool that provides key support for central nervous system (CNS) tumor classification. However, diagnostically ambiguous pediatric cases may result in discordant outputs across classifiers. We developed MAGIBU, a cross-platform, projection-based framework that embeds individual methylomes into a fixed CNS reference landscape, ranking diagnostic entities by local epigenetic proximity to support clinician-led integrative diagnosis. Methods: As a proof-of-concept, we evaluated MAGIBU in eight morphologically challenging pediatric/juvenile CNS tumors with
papers.summary: The authors developed MAGIBU, a cross-platform framework that projects individual DNA methylation profiles onto a fixed CNS tumor reference landscape to aid in classifying challenging pediatric and juvenile CNS tumors. In a proof-of-concept with eight morphologically difficult cases, MAGIBU provided an in-house epigenetic decision-support tool that complements existing online methylation classifiers, potentially reducing diagnostic ambiguity.

papers.title: Nanopore and EPIC array profiling unmask an atypical non-midline H3 K27-altered glioma: a case report.
papers.abstract: We report a rare case of Diffuse Midline Glioma, H3K27-altered, arising in a non-midline fronto-temporo-insular location in a 48-year-old adult, initially mimicking Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, based on radiology and histopathology. Integrated molecular diagnostics, including genome-wide DNA methylation profiling and Sanger sequencing, confirmed an H3.3 K27M mutation, while Nanopore-based methylation profiling provided a rapid and fully concordant classification, demonstrating the feasibility of real-time epigenomic diagnostics in clinical practice. H3K27M-mutant diffuse non-midline gliomas (DN
papers.summary: This case report describes a rare H3 K27-altered glioma arising in a non-midline brain location in an adult, initially misdiagnosed as glioblastoma. Using Nanopore-based methylation profiling alongside standard methods, the authors achieved rapid and accurate molecular classification, highlighting the clinical utility of real-time epigenomic diagnostics for challenging glioma cases.

papers.title: Weighted epigenetic site correlation network analysis of chemotherapy impacts on osteosarcoma cancer survivors' male fertility, sperm, and endocrine parameters.
papers.abstract: The impacts of chemotherapy exposure on adolescent male osteosarcoma survivors as adults were investigated using a number of physiological parameters, with a focus on chemotherapy, reproduction, and sperm. The Children's Oncology Group (COG) clinical sites (protocol ALTE16C1) of previously collected and stored sperm samples were obtained for this analysis. The epigenetic DNA methylation alterations in sperm were assessed in 176 control adult male patients' sperm, and 183 chemotherapy-exposed osteosarcoma survivors' adult male sperm were provided by COG sites. The current study used a weighted
papers.summary: This study examines how chemotherapy affects the sperm epigenome and fertility of adult male survivors of adolescent osteosarcoma, using DNA methylation data from a large cohort. The authors apply weighted epigenetic site correlation network analysis to identify methylation patterns associated with reproductive and endocrine outcomes, providing insights into long-term chemotherapy impacts.

papers.title: The TCN1 Paradox: Unraveling the Dual Role of Transcobalamin I in Colorectal Cancer-From Metabolic Regulation to Oncogenic Signaling.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a leading cause of cancer mortality. While genetic drivers are well-characterized, epigenetic alterations-particularly DNA methylation-are increasingly recognized as critical contributors. The vitamin B12 transporter Transcobalamin I (TCN1) has recently emerged as an epigenetically regulated gene with context-dependent oncogenic functions.
papers.summary: This review discusses the emerging dual role of Transcobalamin I (TCN1) in colorectal cancer, highlighting how its epigenetic regulation, particularly DNA methylation, contributes to context-dependent oncogenic functions beyond its known role as a vitamin B12 transporter. The paper synthesizes current evidence to propose that TCN1 acts as a link between metabolic regulation and oncogenic signaling, offering a new perspective on CRC pathogenesis.
